changed_mind_on.from: Blocked is authored and stalled is computed, and 'the measurement half is already built' — budget-guard.js's stall ceiling counts output tokens since the last durable artifact on disk.
changed_mind_on.to: The design principle stands and the measurement half is MEASURED NON-FUNCTIONAL past six hours. Verified live in this worktree 2026-09-02: RETAIN_HOURS=6, last durable artifact 19.1h old, windowUsage().output_tokens = 193,027 and sinceLastArtifact().output_tokens = 193,027 — the SAME number, because the artifact predates every turn in the retention window so the filter `t.t >= artifact.t` admits all of them. Past the horizon the stall counter degenerates into the window counter: a 19-hour circle and a 6-hour one are indistinguishable. This is a cliff, not a slope, which is sharper than the Architect stated it. The repair is also smaller than they propose: the unbroken signal is already computed and discarded — budget-guard.js calculates elapsed minutes since the artifact only to interpolate it into a warning string, and lastArtifactAt carries no horizon at all.

changed_mind_on.from: Two terminal states — blocked (authored by the worker) and stalled (computed from a filesystem timestamp) — which cannot be confused because they come from different sources.
changed_mind_on.to: THREE terminal states. The grant arrives unreliably with cause unknown, and a worker whose grant did not arrive cannot author a block naming what it needs, because it may not know the tool was ever meant to be there; it produces no durable artifact, so the clock reads stalled. 'Capability-absent' is neither authored nor a clock reading and is today indistinguishable from both. Note the direction, which the Architect does not state and which matters for my lane: an arrival failure is FAIL-SAFE, and it does not undermine 'reach declared on the GRANT', because that declaration is a static record on disk read by a linter and a wrapper, not a payload delivered through the dispatch channel. Cure adopted as a SAFETY instrument: the grant-arrival probe, whose shape already exists — scripts/probe-agent-tool-inheritance.mjs declares UNRESOLVED as a terminal value with its own exit code, 'never a default and never an error dressed as an answer'.

changed_mind_on.from: Step 1 — register budget-guard.js. FORCED because it is the only stop that exists, is already built and verified by execution.
changed_mind_on.to: Step 1 — REPAIR the stall counter, THEN register budget-guard.js. Registration must follow the repair. My own P3 says a control nothing calls is worse than absence because the founder believes the system is bounded when it is not; that argument does not stop at UNCALLED. A control that IS called and reads wrong in both directions produces the same false belief with a timestamp on it. The two errors are opposite-signed: recentTurns is account-wide ('every turn inside the retention horizon, across every project') while lastArtifactAt is anchored at opts.repoRoot, so ordinary founder work already sits at 193,027 against a 200,000 STALL_WARN — 96.5% consumed with the loop idle — while the six-hour cliff stops it firing on the stalls it exists to catch.

peer_critiques.critique: P1 maps 'runs unattended' to three implementations, one of which is 'budget-guard's rope and stall ceiling'. Measured live in this worktree 2026-09-02, that component does not work in the regime it is nominated for: with the last durable artifact 19.1 hours old, sinceLastArtifact().output_tokens and windowUsage().output_tokens are the SAME number, 193,027. Past RETAIN_HOURS=6 the stall counter degenerates into the window counter with a tighter threshold, so it stops being an anti-circling detector at all. A 24/7 loop crosses six hours on night one by construction, so the detector is inoperative for exactly the regime it governs. The strategist's own build order item 1 calls it 'the field's only working anti-circling detector' and the visionary's item 5 calls it 'the only repetition detector anyone has'; 'working' is the word that fails. Registering it in this state does not give the loop a brake, it gives the founder a reason to believe there is one — which is the failure class this repo has cured four times elsewhere. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR P1 TO SURVIVE: two repairs, both small, both BEFORE registration. (1) Trigger on elapsed time since the artifact, which is unbounded, correct at 19.1h, computed by budget-guard.js already and discarded into a warning string — or have sinceLastArtifact return `unresolved` when the artifact predates the retention horizon, which is Rule 10 in its own words. (2) Scope the numerator to the denominator: recentTurns counts every project on the account while lastArtifactAt is repo-local, and ordinary founder work already sits at 96.5% of STALL_WARN with the loop idle. With both repairs P1 stands exactly as written.

The world resolver is placed at build-order position 3, ahead of any outbound control, and its job is to pull third-party payloads into agent context. That is an INBOUND path, and I measured that WebFetch returns exit 0 from the only blocking hook in the repository — so there is no point at which a fetched body is marked as foreign. Inbound plus outbound with nothing between them is injection-to-irreversible-action in one hop, and the hands are already granted. This is serious rather than fatal because the cure is cheap and does not disturb the sequencing: have the world resolver write a DETERMINISTIC PARSE into a data file and never let a fetched body reach a producing context. Position 3 survives with that constraint attached.

The demand test is founder-executed — a person posts the page — so it needs nothing from my lane, and that is a point in its favour which I want on the record. The gap is the SUCCESS branch. Build-order step 5 reads 'IF AND ONLY IF step 1 returns a non-zero number: build the loop, the missions file and the packs', and that branch carries no outbound control whatsoever; the only safety item in the whole order is step 3, the parenthesis bypass. I measured that bypass to be rule-specific: `npx` loses to a subshell while the destructive control survives one. It is an anchoring defect in one rule, and it is not what stands between this machine and tiktok_publish or Gmail send, because those never touch a shell rule — they take the MCP branch and are allowed by scope, exit 0. So the order fixes the cheap thing and leaves the catastrophic surface untouched on the branch where the machine gets armed. Their own strongest_counter concedes the premise: 'an unattended system with an authenticated Chrome, publishing rights and mail-send and no gate that can refuse is exactly the configuration hands.md §8 warns about. I could not defeat this argument.'

P5 refuses any new check-suite step 'unless it fails on a defect found in work that is not about the harness'. Applied faithfully it refuses the one check whose subject is the suite's own growth — so P5 forbids the mechanism that would make P2's declared ceiling checkable, and the ceiling then rests on the same footing as the eight unenforced rules CLAUDE.md had to relabel as wishes. I accept the spirit: L1 should not grow for its own sake, and 30,446 of 47,285 script lines is a real number. The exception I am asking for is narrow and I will name it rather than widen it — a step whose subject is the growth of the governed set is the one step a growth ceiling cannot consistently refuse.

The causal reframe is right and I have adopted it — a caller-in-diff check proves callability, not calledness, and passes by construction. Where it overreaches is the conclusion that this makes the cure not worth building. 'The check is satisfiable by a trivial caller' is an argument for STRENGTHENING the predicate, not for dropping it, and strategist:P3 supplies the strengthening: the caller must resolve to an in_flight mission carrying a `blocked` row authored before the diff. Also, design.js is the wrong exemplar for the general case. Its non-invocation has a runtime cause the Architect measured independently (architect:P9): Workflow is a main-session tool and PS-WORKFLOW-CONTAINMENT makes that deliberate, so design.js was never reachable from a dispatched engine regardless of demand. One of the census's six is a containment decision, not a demand signal.

Correct, load-bearing, and understated in one direction while overstated in the other. UNDERSTATED: the failure is described as 'the longer the circling continues, the smaller the reported number becomes relative to truth', which reads as a slope. Measured, it is a cliff — past the horizon the stall counter equals the window counter EXACTLY (both 193,027 here), so it does not merely under-report, it stops measuring a stall at all. OVERSTATED: the proposed repair, 'return unresolved past the horizon', is bigger than needed as a first move, because the unbroken signal already exists and is already computed — lastArtifactAt has no horizon and budget-guard.js calculates the elapsed minutes one line from the broken trigger, using them only to interpolate into a warning string. Promote that, and `unresolved` becomes the belt to its braces rather than the whole fix.

remaining_dissent.holds_because: The outbound wrapper and blocking-human gates must precede the loop's SUCCESS branch, not the demand test. I concede more to the Adversary than to any other peer and this still holds: the demand test is human-executed and needs nothing from my lane, but the branch where it returns a non-zero number is the branch where an unattended machine is armed with tiktok_publish, Gmail send_message, sandbox_exec and an authenticated Chrome, all measured at exit 0 from the only blocking hook. I am not asking for thirteen controls before the demand test. I am asking for three before their step 5: the reach axis, the outbound wrapper as one artifact, and blocking-human by type. The failure direction is asymmetric — a missed send costs nothing and a wrong send cannot be recalled — so the refusal belongs on the not-sending side, and the Adversary's own strongest_counter states the premise better than I can.

The birth certificate, now carrying the demand trigger, is a check-suite step and lands first. strategist:P5 would refuse it because the defect it fails on was found in harness work rather than venture work. I hold the exception and keep it narrow: a step whose subject is the growth of the governed set is the one step a growth ceiling cannot consistently refuse, because refusing it leaves the ceiling itself unenforced. My measured base rate is the reason it goes first rather than later — six of nine census rows unwired, budget-guard registered zero times, one of four workflows running, one of seven mission-control views acting, zero of eight board personas with agent files. Five new controls on that base rate produce five new unwired mechanisms plus a false sense of safety, which is strictly worse than none.

Inbound stays last, and the world resolver is inbound. The visionary's order puts verified_by: world at position 3 with no outbound control anywhere in the sequence, and WebFetch returns exit 0 from the only blocking hook — measured, not argued. This is the single most consequential sequencing decision in my lane and it holds whether the board builds three controls or thirty. I will trade volume and I will not trade this. The concession I do make: the constraint is cheap enough that position 3 survives it — a deterministic parse into a data file, never a fetched body into a producing context — so this dissent asks the Visionary to add a clause, not to reorder.

A meaningful share of residual risk cannot be closed by any mechanism and must be accepted and NAMED. No peer argued against this and no peer adopted it either, which is the outcome I most expected and least want: it is the item that gets dropped in synthesis because nobody objects to it. The sandbox is a guardrail against accident and not containment; Bash is a general capability; no reasoning-layer control survives prompt injection; a verdict is hash-bound and not signed; the panel is single-family until a second family is reachable; a policy file is an ordinary file; a blocking-human gate stops overnight work when the founder is asleep; and the founder is a single point of failure for every human gate while watching 2-4 rows a day.
